rationale: Official record first posted 2024-03-07; completed, no structured results. Black cumin oil is applied topically in massage/reflexology for knee osteoarthritis pain and fatigue. Exposure is Nigella-related, but no apathy/motivation endpoint, no Parkinson population, and no oral ground black seed exposure; pain is outside the mapped lovage pain claim as the exposure differs.

Official record first posted 2023-04-25; completed, no structured results. DailyColors is a 150-mg multi-ingredient blend including blueberry, kale, rosemary and grapefruit extracts/powders. Registered outcomes are blood CD38/NAD+, inflammation, antioxidant capacity, 4-HNE and protein carbonyl in healthy adults, not voice, olfaction, tremor or stride length; individual-food effects are not separable. A credited trial report exists, but does not make these mapped endpoints a match.

Official record first posted 2024-06-05; active, not recruiting; no structured results. Secukinumab observational follow-up for hidradenitis suppurativa includes patient-rated bad smell and quality-of-life symptoms, but no chervil exposure and no depression endpoint. “Bad smell” is not olfactory impairment.

Official record first posted 2019-04-30; active, not recruiting; no structured results. Sulforaphane versus placebo is studied for psychosis risk in high-risk participants. No assigned chervil or kale; psychosis-risk conversion and prodromal symptoms are not depression outcomes or olfactory function. Broccoli-derived compound relation is indirect and not a registered kale exposure.

Official record first posted 2014-11-19; status UNKNOWN; no structured results. Qishe Pill pharmacokinetics is a multi-ingredient traditional medicine study; neither chervil nor depression is registered as exposure/outcome. “Unknown” status is the registry status, not evidence of a positive or negative result.

Official record first posted 2025-10-27; recruiting; no structured results. BOOST assigns conventional smell training with clove as one of four odors (and a scented-marker arm) in adults with HIV; outcomes include olfaction and Trail Making Test B. This is an odor-exposure/cognition lead with a potentially relevant executive-function measure, but clove is not administered as food/spice and the registry does not name executive function as the endpoint; no Parkinson population or posted results.

Official record first posted 2026-09-25; completed; no structured results. CBD versus placebo in multiple sclerosis measures sleep quality/insomnia. No soybean-oil exposure or daytime sleepiness endpoint; this is a lexical “sleep” collision.

Official record first posted 2022-07-07; completed; no structured results. A complementary-care bundle for colorectal surgery includes aromatherapy and hand massage with sleep, anxiety, pain and perioperative measures. Almond oil is not the assigned intervention and falls are not an outcome.

Official record first posted 2023-11-27; completed; no structured results. A melatonin/magnesium lotion study assesses sleep quality and wearable sleep duration. Almond oil appears as a lotion constituent/intervention-name lexical hit, but not soybean oil; no daytime sleepiness endpoint.

Official record first posted 2021-03-22; completed; no structured results. Aromatherapy massage for colorectal cancer symptom control does not assign spearmint or measure olfactory impairment; this is an aromatherapy lexical collision.

Official record first posted 2025-02-12; not yet recruiting; no structured results. Modified versus conventional olfactory training is registered for older adults at risk of MCI; clove appears among conventional/participant-selected odors in the trial description, and outcomes include smell identification plus broad cognition (including MoCA, AVLT, Stroop-adjacent tests). It is not a clove-spice intervention, does not register Parkinson’s executive function as the target, and has no posted results. Treat as indirect scent/cognitive context.

Official record first posted 2025-10-03; completed; no structured results. Pediatric surgical treatment for combined fecal/urinary incontinence assesses complications and quality of life. “MACE” is Malone antegrade continent enema, not chives; no apathy or pain-severity claim outcome.

Official first posting 2013-10-11, completed with structured results. The assessments use an alertness/sedation scale during endoscopy. The drug code EES0000645/A does not map to claim 0645. No assigned refined culinary soybean oil or Parkinson daytime sleepiness comparison is established.

Official record first posted 2021-01-14; completed; no structured results on ClinicalTrials.gov. In the COVID-related loss-of-smell VOLT trial, clove is one assigned conventional odor and can be chosen from the preferred odor list; UPSIT and other smell-loss outcomes are measured. No Parkinson population, no executive-function endpoint for the mapped clove claim, and no spearmint-specific effect. Credited companion RCT reports actual olfactory outcomes (Lee et al., PMID 36649132; PMC9857399), so this is a verified adjacent clove/smell report, not a direct claim match.
